mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over the prior three months signals a tightening monetary regime, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% q/q over last 3 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods where FEDFUNDS rises >0.25% q/q.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the unemployment rate below 5% for two consecutive months signals a late-cycle labor market tightening, which reduces slack and increases wage pressures, compressing profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE is below 5% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A sequential decline in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) for two consecutive months signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both fall for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative when both GDPC1 and HOUST decline for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly contraction in the industrial production index (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for three consecutive months signals supply-side weakness, which raises input costs and reduces output, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative when INDPRO is below its 12-month MA for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above its 12-month moving average, combined with a simultaneous decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE), signals a tight labor market that accelerates wage growth and erodes profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 12-month MA and UNRATE falls in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative when PAYEMS exceeds its 12-month MA and UNRATE declines in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 2.5% for three consecutive months signals entrenched inflation, prompting expectations of aggressive monetary tightening, which reduces equity valuations and yields negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative when CPIAUCSL exceeds 2.5% for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp reduction in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 1% combined with a concurrent decline in real personal savings (RSAFS) signals accommodative policy and reduced household savings, which boosts consumption and supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 1.0% AND RSAFS declines for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly positive when FEDFUNDS < 1% and RSAFS declines for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent, unbroken monthly increase in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) for six consecutive months signals robust aggregate demand expansion, which supports corporate earnings growth and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days regardless of regime.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly positive during any 6-month stretch where GDPC1 rises every month.
